name: sed
summary: Transforms a stream of text line by line.
description: Stream EDitor: reads text line by line, applies a script to it (substitution, deletion, insertion…) and writes the result. The most common command is substitution, s/old/new/. By default, the original file is not changed: the result goes to standard output.

options.description: Edits the file directly instead of printing the result. -i.bak keeps a backup copy.
Does not print every line automatically; only lines requested with the p command are printed.
Adds a script; lets you chain several commands.
Reads the script from a file.
Extended regular expressions (+, ?, |, () without backslashes). -r is the same.

arguments.name: SCRIPT
arguments.description: sed commands: s/pattern/replacement/g replaces, /pattern/d deletes, 5p prints line 5…

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: File(s) to process. Without a file: standard input.

examples.explanation: Replaces the first occurrence of “cat” on each line.
The g flag replaces every occurrence on each line.

dangerNote: With -i, the file is changed with no way back. Test without -i first, or use -i.bak to keep a copy.
